policies.description: Ranks investigations by EIG/(cost+λ·time), stops when one source reaches 60%, gets human approvals, rejects claim-only closure, requires an independent measurement, re-plans after failed repairs, and reopens on recurrence.

definitions.false_closure: Case closed AND (no independent VERIFIED_REDUCTION verdict behind the closure OR the hidden true emission was not actually reduced, i.e. true post ≥ 0.5·E0). Target: 0.
definitions.closed: The case reached a closed/resolved state at some point (a later automatic reopen does not undo the count; see final_status = RECURRING).
definitions.resolved: The operator's repair actually hit the hidden true source and was effective (true emission reduced), regardless of the paperwork.
definitions.inspections: Field inspections: OGI surveys, ground surveys and independent measurement campaigns (actions with is_field_inspection). Records requests and satellite waits are not inspections.
definitions.attribution_inspections_per_case: Field inspections used to IDENTIFY THE SOURCE (OGI + ground surveys; excludes verification campaigns), mean per case. PDF objective 2.
definitions.cost_per_resolved_inr: Total investigation + verification cost (₹) / resolved cases.
definitions.days_to_stakeholder: Simulated days from detection until the accountable operator is formally identified and assigned (A: alert forwarded by the national focal point; B: manual lookup; C: overlay + approval).
definitions.traceability_pct: % of critical decisions (investigation, attribution, notification, closure) that link the evidence their kind requires (investigation→observation, attribution→finding, notification→attribution decision, closure→independent VERIFIED_REDUCTION verdict) AND have a recorded human approval.
definitions.correct_attribution_rate: Share of all cases where the policy's final attributed source equals the hidden true source (A never attributes → 0).
definitions.mean_days_to_closure: Mean simulated day of closure, over cases that were closed.

notes: All 25 scenarios, operator behaviour, inspector availability, records content and measurements are SIMULATED. Likelihoods, costs and delays are illustrative demonstration values (docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md).
Fairness: each scenario's world answers and measurement noise are pre-sampled once, so every policy faces the same world.
Recurrence scenarios: 5. Automatically reopened after closure: A: Alert-only 0, B: Fixed checklist 0, C: PlumeProof 5, C-ablation: planner disabled 5. A and B do no post-closure monitoring.

Field inspections used for SOURCE ATTRIBUTION only (excluding verification campaigns), mean per case: A: Alert-only 0.00, B: Fixed checklist 1.80, C: PlumeProof 0.72, C-ablation: planner disabled 0.84. PlumeProof's totals above also include its independent verification campaigns, which A and B never pay for.
A and B close on the operator's repair claim, so every closure they make is a false closure by definition (no independent evidence). This follows from their design; it is not a tuned result.
Measurement noise is bounded (|error| ≤ 0.8·u). With unbounded (e.g. Gaussian) noise, rare false verified reductions become possible for any policy that relies on measurements.
